name: Bebe Nanaki
role: Guru Nanak's elder sister and first follower
summary: Bebe Nanaki (c. 1464–1518) was Guru Nanak's elder sister. She was the first to recognise his spiritual greatness, and Sikhs often call her the first Sikh.
about: Sikh sources say Nanaki was born around 1464 in Chahal village, in present-day Pakistani Punjab, to Mehta Kalu and Mata Tripta, about five years before her brother. Sikh sources call her the first person to see his spiritual greatness. In 1475 she married Jai Ram, who worked in the Nawab's storehouse at Sultanpur Lodhi. When Nanak came to Sultanpur, he lived in her home and Jai Ram helped him find work. She and Jai Ram also helped arrange his marriage to Sulakhani and she loved his sons Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das as her own, since she had no children. She died at Sultanpur in 1518 with her brother beside her, and Jai Ram died three days later. She should not be confused with Mata Nanaki, wife of Guru Hargobind. 'Bebe' is a respectful word for an older woman.
kidSummary: Bebe Nanaki was Guru Nanak's big sister, and she was the very first person to see how special he was. She acted like a second mother to him, helped him find a home in Sultanpur, and loved his children as her own.

story.title: A big sister
story.text: Nanaki was born about five years before her brother Nanak. Even when they were small, she noticed that he thought deeply about God.

story.title: Married to Jai Ram
story.text: In 1475 she married Jai Ram, who worked at the Nawab's storehouse in Sultanpur Lodhi. Their house later became a second home for her brother.

story.title: A home for Nanak
story.text: When Nanak came to Sultanpur, he stayed with her. Jai Ram helped him find a job, and the two of them helped him find a bride.

story.title: A loving aunt
story.text: Nanaki had no children of her own, so she loved Nanak's sons, Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das, as if they were hers.

story.title: Brother by her side
story.text: In 1518 she asked her brother to stay with her for a little longer. She died with him near, and Jai Ram passed away three days later.

teaches: Family love that believes in someone first
Looking after those who need care

facts.text: She was married in 1475 at about eleven, then stayed with her parents' family until she was grown. She joined her husband Jai Ram in Sultanpur when she was around sixteen.
Her maternal grandparents named her Nanaki, from a word for the home of one's mother's parents, where she was born. Later her little brother was named Nanak after her.
Wikipedia says Nanak was sent to live with Nanaki at fifteen. To help him stand on his own feet she searched for a bride, and she and Jai Ram found Sulakhni.
Wikipedia credits her with inspiring Nanak's use of music as devotion, and says she bought him a rebab, which fits the later story of the rabab-playing Mardana.
Sikh tradition says Nanak went into the Kali Bein stream at Sultanpur and vanished for three days. He reappeared at Sant Ghat with a message that placed no wall between Hindu and Muslim.
Nanak told her he could stay only three days at his last visit. She fell ill on the second day and died on the third, in his arms, as he recited the Japji. Jai Ram died three days later.
Jai Ram worked at a modikhana, a government storehouse for revenue paid in goods rather than cash. Nanak later took a post in that storehouse at Sultanpur.
Wikipedia notes that her original house at Sultanpur Lodhi was lost when 21st-century kar seva renovations replaced it with a modern building.
Gurdwara Bebe Nanaki at Sultanpur Lodhi was built from a cornerstone laid on 13 November 1970 by a charitable trust whose chair, Bibi Balvant Kaur, was based in Birmingham in the United Kingdom.
The same gurdwara keeps a small side room where the Guru Granth Sahib is also seated, standing for Bebe Nanaki's own lodging.
Kaur Life says Nanak travelled for about 25 years but visited his sister between journeys, and he promised to come to her if she ever needed him.
When Nanak left on his travels, Kaur Life says Nanaki took over the care of his eldest son, Siri Chand.

quiz.q: What did Bebe Nanaki buy for her brother, which fits the later rabab story?
quiz.why: Wikipedia says she bought him a rebab and inspired his use of music in devotion.

quiz.q: In which town did Bebe Nanaki live with her husband Jai Ram?
quiz.why: Nanak came to live with her in Sultanpur Lodhi.

quiz.q: Whose sons did Bebe Nanaki care for as her own?
quiz.why: She loved Sri Chand and Lakhmi Das, Nanak's sons, as her own.

quiz.q: Who died three days after Bebe Nanaki?
quiz.why: Her husband Jai Ram died three days later.
